advisory.finding: The per-test budget guard and the `SCRIPT_RUN_TIMEOUT` comment both assume at most two script runs per test, but several tests run the script three times in a row. Three runs can now take up to 3 x 135 = 405 s, more than pytest's 300 s per-test budget (before this change: 3 x 60 = 180 s). On a slow or hung third run, pytest-timeout's thread method ends the xdist worker with `os._exit` before `run_observability`'s `except BaseException` can kill the process group. That leaves the script's process group orphaned, which is the outcome the commit says it rules out.
scenarios: Under heavy CI contention, each run in a three-run test takes about 100-110 s. Every run stays inside its own bound, but the total passes 300 s, so pytest-timeout kills the worker (`node down`) instead of reporting a clean TimeoutExpired.
The third run of the mcp_health latch test really hangs after two loaded runs of about 90 s each. The pytest budget fires before the 135 s bound, and the group-reap path never runs.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `@pytest.mark.timeout(450)` with a one-line reason to each test that runs the script three times (mcp_health_9ea3 latch test, mirror_sync_bff5 replication test, and any others). Alternatively, change the guard to `MAX_RUNS_PER_TEST * SCRIPT_RUN_TIMEOUT < budget` with `MAX_RUNS_PER_TEST = 3` and lower the tier so 3 x tier < 300, and fix the comment.

merged_from: The new tests only enforce part of what they claim. The docstring says every whole-script run must use SCRIPT_RUN_TIMEOUT, and the budget test says a test that runs the script twice must fail on its own bound. But the scan rejects only the value 60, and the budget check reads only the constant. Whole-script runs still bounded by literal 120/180 pass both tests, including one test that makes two 180 s runs (360 s) against the 300 s pytest budget.
